issues.legal_issue: A party may challenge an earlier judgment as fraudulent or collusive in a later proceeding without first bringing an independent suit to set it aside.
material_facts: A party relied on an earlier injunction decree in later statutory proceedings concerning common land.
The Panchayat alleged that the earlier decree had been obtained through collusion with its then representative.
The statutory authorities found collusion, but the High Court allowed a writ petition on the ground that an independent suit was required first.
The High Court did not examine the merits of the statutory authorities’ decision.
issues.conclusion: The statutory authorities could consider whether the earlier decree was collusive without requiring the Panchayat first to bring an independent suit. The contrary Full Bench rule was incorrect; the High Court’s judgment was set aside and the writ petition remitted for disposal in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Section 44 of the Indian Evidence Act permits a party to show in a later proceeding that a relevant judgment was obtained by fraud or collusion; it does not make a prior independent suit to set the judgment aside a condition precedent. This accords with the authorities collected in Sarkar’s Evidence Act, including Bansi v. Dhapo, Rajib v. Lakhan, Parbati v. Gajraj, Prayag v. Siva, Hare Krishna v. Umesh, Aswini v. Banamali, Manchharam v. Kalidas, Ranganath v. Govind, Kamiruddin v. Jhadejanessa, Bhagwandas v. Patel & Co., Bishunath v. Mirchi, and Vijaya v. Padmanabham. The Court also relied on Spencer-Bower and Turner on Res Judicata and the principle that fraud or collusion may defeat an estoppel without active proceedings to rescind the earlier judgment. Section 11 CPC is relevant to the asserted res judicata bar.

predicates.collateral_proceeding: A party raises an objection to an earlier judgment in a later proceeding rather than in a separate action to set that judgment aside.
predicates.earlier_judgment_invoked_as_bar: A party relies on the earlier judgment as a bar or as the basis of an estoppel in the later proceeding.
predicates.collusion_or_fraud_alleged: A party alleges that the earlier judgment was obtained through fraud or collusion.

issues.definition: When a party in a later proceeding relies on an earlier judgment as a bar and the opposing party alleges fraud or collusion, that allegation may be raised without first bringing a separate suit.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier judgment in an injunction suit does not bind a later proceeding on title unless deciding title was necessary to grant or refuse the injunction and the relief was based on that title determination.
material_facts: The earlier suit sought an injunction and was not a suit on title.
The earlier decision did not decide title.
The later proceedings directly concerned title to the property.
issues.conclusion: The earlier injunction decree could not bind the parties on title because title had not been decided in that suit. An incidental title finding would not bind a later proceeding in which title is directly in issue unless deciding title was necessary to the injunction and the relief was based on that finding.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11 CPC, an incidental finding on title in an earlier injunction suit is not binding in a later proceeding where title is directly in issue unless it was necessary to decide title to grant or refuse the injunction and the relief was founded on that title finding. The Court relied on Sajjadanashin Sayed v. Musa Dadabhai Ummer, (2000) 3 SCC 350.

rule.if: later_proceeding_directly_puts_title_in_issue and earlier_suit_sought_only_injunction and (not title_finding_necessary or not injunction_relief_based_on_title)

predicates.later_proceeding_directly_puts_title_in_: The later proceeding directly requires determination of title to the property.
predicates.earlier_suit_sought_only_injunction: The earlier suit sought an injunction rather than a determination of title.
predicates.title_finding_necessary: A finding on title was necessary to grant or refuse the injunction in the earlier suit.
predicates.injunction_relief_based_on_title: The relief granted or refused in the earlier suit was founded on the title finding.

issues.definition: When a later proceeding directly concerns title and the earlier suit sought only an injunction, the earlier judgment does not bind on title if deciding title was unnecessary or the injunction relief was not based on that decision.
